pr_title: Use Empty instead of null for DCS deserializing namespace.
pr_body:
DCS: Allow RootName without RootNamespace when deserializing

DCS will allow users to specify a custom RootName for serializing without also
specifying a custom RootNamespace if the DCS is created from
DataContractSerializerSettings. In this case, the root namespace is simply
left out and the xml gets generated without a root namespace. Going
the other way through deserialization fails though because DCS passes
'null' as the expected namespace and the XmlReader classes are calling
the absence of an explicitly given namespace '' - aka, the empty string.

Fixes #41395

issue_context.title: NullReferenceException in DataContractSerializer
comments:
The example here is actually setting _RootName_ and not _RootName**space**_. There is no exception when setting the root namespace to the empty string, and the behavior in that case is the same as it was in 4.8.

When setting RootName however, I believe this exception is the same as it was in 4.8 as well. Which makes sense because how do you read or write an xml element whose name is ""?

> The example here is actually setting RootName and not RootNamespace. 

Correct - that is the point of this bug. 

_Not setting DataContractSerializerSettings.RootNamespace can cause NullReferenceExceptions in DataContractSerializer._

Oh, so you mean that you get an error when you specify a valid RootName without specifying a RootNamespace? The empty string is definitely not valid as a RootName, so I was getting an expected error for that reason with your sample. I see the error you're mentioning here now.

FWIW, this error is also still the same as 4.8. Though I am able to serialize successfully with these settings before failing on the deserializing leg. So we could look at fixing this to improve the round-trip experience.

Yeah, setting RootName to empty wasn’t really relevant here - it just needed to be set to some non-null value to illustrate the NRE when not setting RootNamespace.

note - I found this bug when I was annotating the XmlSerializer with nullable annotations. It isn’t high priority to fix, but should be pretty simple. So maybe marking it as “up for grabs” might make sense.

review_comments: Is it worth modifying the null check on name to also check that it isn't equivalent to l to XmlDictionaryString.Empty? If you do that, it might be worth checking `name.Value.Length != 0` as someone can make their own XmlDictionaryString with the empty string and then the equality comparison won't work with XmlDictionaryString.Empty

Interestingly, we don't check the rootname or rootnamespace arguments for validity when constructing DCS. So somebody could totally create an empty rootname. But I think that's an error that should be dealt with in user code, even if we could validate a little better. I don't think this is the place or the issue to address that pit of success.
